title: Laser Pistol
textLines: Your pulse quickens as the clanking grows louder.
Whatever's coming, it's not subtle—and it's getting close.
You grab the laser pistol from its mount, thumb brushing over the setting dial.
You make sure it's set to stun. No sense killing someone if it's just crew.
The footsteps echo closer through the corridor.
Metal grinds.
A faint, rasping breath.
You raise the weapon, muscles tight, aiming toward the open doorway. The emergency lights flicker—red, then dark, then red again.
A figure steps into view. Human-shaped.
Before you can think, your finger squeezes the trigger.
A sharp pulse of blue light lances through the air.
The shot hits square in the chest.
The figure jerks violently, a strangled cry tearing free—then collapses.
For a moment you think they're just stunned. Then the smell hits you.
A bitter, chemical tang—burnt ozone and scorched flesh.
The body twitches once, then goes still. Wisps of smoke curl up from blackened fabric.
You blink, staring down at the weapon.
Stun. The indicator still glows soft blue.
You check it again—definitely stun.
Then why—?
You take a hesitant step forward. The emergency lights stutter, painting the corridor in pulses of red and shadow.
The person's skin has blackened in strange, uneven patches—almost melted in places, cracked like old glass.
Whatever the shot did, it burned deep, too deep for a stun pulse.
And yet… beneath the charring, the shape of the face—it feels… familiar. You can't tell why. The features are warped difficult to make out.
You pull back, chest tight.
That wasn't just a malfunction. Something else happened when you fired.
The ship groans then, a deep, resonant shudder that rattles the walls.
Somewhere in the hull, metal creaks under strain.
The deck hums faintly beneath your boots, like a pulse traveling through the ship itself.
The silence that follows is almost unbearable.
You take a hesitant step closer. The air around the body still wavers with residual heat.
A low vibration thrums through the floor again, stronger this time. Somewhere, deep in the ship, something heavy shifts.
You can't stay here.
You glance back down at the corpse one last time.
Maybe they have something useful—something that explains what just happened.
Or maybe you should move before the ship decides to tear itself apart.
What do you do?
1. Search the body. There might be something that helps you understand what's going on.
2. Keep moving. Figure out what's causing the ship to buckle before you end up like them.
